title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right thigh at the adductor canal, as on the screen with the probe on the medial thigh: vastus medialis (lateral) on the image left, adductor longus on the right.
teachingPoint: Under the sartorius, the saphenous nerve lies beside the femoral artery in the canal; needle in-plane from lateral, spread in the plane around the artery and nerve.
claims: Right thigh at the adductor canal, lateral on the left (NYSORA's plate, concept only).
Saphenous nerve with the femoral artery deep to the sartorius, anterolateral to the artery (record).
Femoral vein deep to the artery; vastus medialis lateral, adductor longus medial (standard anatomy).
Needle in-plane from lateral, tip beside the nerve at the artery's plane (record).
Teal: spread in the fascial plane around the nerve, against the artery's lateral wall (record: the plane around the artery).
Labels: Sartorius, Saphenous nerve, Femoral artery, Femoral vein, Vastus medialis.

geometry.why: nerve lateral to the artery (lateral is left)
nerve in the canal, not in muscle
tip beside, not in, the nerve
